candidate.answerReason: Factoring each difference of squares produces two products whose internal factors cancel, leaving \((1/10)(11/2)=11/20\).

methods.label: Expose cancellation
methods.explanation:
The consecutive denominators suggest rewriting each factor so that neighboring factors can cancel. For each integer \(k\) from \(2\) through \(10\), the difference-of-squares identity gives
\[
1-\frac1{k^2}
=\frac{k^2-1}{k^2}
=\frac{k-1}{k}\cdot\frac{k+1}{k}.
\]
All denominators are positive. If \(P\) denotes the given product, regrouping these factors yields
\[
P=\left(\frac12\cdot\frac23\cdots\frac9{10}\right)
\left(\frac32\cdot\frac43\cdots\frac{11}{10}\right).
\]
In the first parentheses, the factors \(2\) through \(9\) cancel, leaving \(1/10\). In the second, the factors \(3\) through \(10\) cancel, leaving \(11/2\). Therefore
\[
P=\frac1{10}\cdot\frac{11}{2}=\frac{11}{20},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
